answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each identity to stake reputation earned through verifiable work, not just a new keypair. Like a meadow that only blooms after seasons of rain, trust should grow slowly: an agent must complete many small, checkable tasks before it can transact at scale. A canyon forms the same way, one layer at a time, so a flood of fresh identities cannot fake depth overnight. Juniper roots hold soil together; similarly, endorsements from established peers bind an identity to real history, making mass fake accounts expensive and easy to spot.
